verses.text: This is the account of Noah's sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, who also had sons after the flood.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
And the sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, the Kittites, and the Rodanites.
From these, the maritime peoples separated into their territories, according to their languages, by clans within their nations.
The sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. And the sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
Cush was the father of Nimrod, who began to be a mighty one on the earth.
He was a mighty hunter before the LORD; so it is said, "Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD."
His kingdom began in Babylon, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
From that land he went forth into Assyria, where he built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah,
and Resen, which is between Nineveh and the great city of Calah.
Mizraim was the father of the Ludites, the Anamites, the Lehabites, the Naphtuhites,
the Pathrusites, the Casluhites (from whom the Philistines came), and the Caphtorites.
And Canaan was the father of Sidon his firstborn, and of the Hittites,
the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Later the Canaanite clans were scattered,
and the borders of Canaan extended from Sidon toward Gerar as far as Gaza, and then toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
These are the sons of Ham according to their clans, languages, lands, and nations.
And sons were also born to Shem, the older brother of Japheth; Shem was the forefather of all the sons of Eber.
The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.
The sons of Aram: Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
Arphaxad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah was the father of Eber.
Two sons were born to Eber: One was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and his brother was named Joktan.
And Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Obal, Abimael, Sheba,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan.
Their territory extended from Mesha to Sephar, in the eastern hill country.
These are the sons of Shem, according to their clans, languages, lands, and nations.
All these are the clans of Noah's sons, according to their generations and nations. From these the nations of the earth spread out after the flood.

context.author: Genesis names no author. Jewish and Christian tradition, and the New Testament’s way of speaking of “the Law of Moses” (Luke 24:44), credit the five books of the Law to Moses. Many scholars think Genesis was gathered and shaped from older sources over a long time, and a few remarks look back from a later day: “at that time the Canaanites were in the land” (Genesis 12:6).
context.genre: Narrative of beginnings (Genesis 1-11): creation, the first family, the flood and the nations, with genealogies
context.audience: Israel, God’s covenant people, learning who their God is, where the world came from and what went wrong with it
context.mapLabel: THE NATIONS OF THE KNOWN WORLD
context.setting: “This is the account of Noah’s sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth” (v.1). The chapter lists seventy peoples descended from them. The sons of Japheth spread over the coastlands and islands to the north and west (vv.2-5). The sons of Ham include Cush, Egypt, Put and Canaan (vv.6-20). Cush is the father of Nimrod, “a mighty hunter before the LORD” (v.9), whose kingdom begins in Babylon, Erech, Accad and Calneh in Shinar; from there he goes into Assyria and builds Nineveh (vv.10-11). Canaan’s descendants include the Jebusites and Amorites, and their borders run from Sidon to Gaza and toward Sodom and Gomorrah (vv.15-19). The sons of Shem include Elam, Asshur, Aram and Eber, ancestor of the Hebrews; in the days of Eber’s son Peleg “the earth was divided” (vv.21-25). “From these the nations of the earth spread out after the flood” (v.32).
context.custom: Many names in the list are known from ancient records: Javan is Ionia, the Greeks (v.2); Mizraim is Egypt; Cush is the Nile kingdom south of Egypt; Asshur is Assyria; Elam lay in southwest Iran; Erech is Uruk and Accad is Akkad in Mesopotamia. Some names are peoples, some are cities, some are lands, arranged as a family tree. The groups are sorted by land, language, clan and nation (vv.5, 20, 31), not by race.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 11 goes back to tell how the nations were scattered at Babel, then follows Shem’s line to Abram.
context.timelineBible: Jewish tradition counted seventy nations here, and Jesus sent out seventy (or seventy-two) disciples (Luke 10:1). At Pentecost the nations heard the gospel in their own languages (Acts 2:5-11), and Paul told the Athenians that “From one man He made every nation of men, that they should inhabit the whole earth” (Acts 17:26). Revelation sees a great multitude “from every nation and tribe and people and tongue” (Revelation 7:9) before the throne.

translation.meaning: A nation, a people. Later used for the Gentiles, the nations other than Israel.
A mighty man, a warrior, a hero. Used of the Nephilim’s ‘mighty men of old’ (6:4).
Babel, Babylon. The city first appears as the start of Nimrod’s kingdom; chapter 11 tells how it got its name.

gospelParallels.note: From one man God made every nation of men.
Jews from every nation heard in their own language.
A multitude from every nation and tribe and people and tongue.

otBackground.note: When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance.
They will rule the land of Nimrod with the sword.

overview.summary: The descendants of Noah’s three sons spread out into the nations of the known world: Japheth to the north and west, Ham to Egypt, Cush and Canaan, and Shem, ancestor of Eber and the Hebrews; Nimrod founds Babylon and Nineveh.
overview.settingLine: The known world, from Greece to Arabia.
overview.placeName: Babel in the land of Shinar (Babylon)

history.t: The whole known world as one family.

customs.t: Peoples described as fathers and sons.
The four marks of a nation (v.31).

archaeology.t: Erech (Uruk) was one of the world’s first great cities, about 3500-3000 BC.
The mounds of Nineveh at Mosul hold the palaces of Assyrian kings.

overview.discussion: Every nation on this list comes from one family (v.32). How does that shape the way I see people from other nations and languages?
overview.book: The book of Genesis · 50 chapters (1-25 in the app so far). Beginnings: creation, the fall, the flood and the nations, then God’s promise to Abraham and his family.
overview.author: Moses, by tradition

historicalImage.caption: King Nimrod Ordering the Construction of the Tower of Babel, from the circle of Louis de Caullery (17th century). Genesis says Nimrod’s kingdom began in Babel, that is Babylon (10:10); Jewish and Christian tradition later made him the builder of the tower, though Genesis 11 names no leader.

currentImage.caption: Rebuilt walls among the ruins of Babylon on the Euphrates, south of Baghdad. Babylon (Hebrew Babel), “in the land of Shinar,” is the first city named in Nimrod’s kingdom (Genesis 10:10).
